decision: Use a deterministic multi-run qualification aggregator over independent raw Qubes campaign event sets, with strict campaign framing and bounded clock-skew validation.
problem: A single canonical qrexec campaign may not produce the minimum recovery and round-trip sample count required for p95 readiness. Aggregation must preserve per-run provenance and must not accept evidence outside explicit campaign boundaries or future-dated evidence that can bypass freshness checks.

reviewers.preferred: multi-run aggregator with unique runId, same SHA/topology enforcement, per-run freshness, strict start/end framing, aggregate scenario coverage, and summed correctness counters
reviewers.reason: preserves independent-run boundaries while preventing pre-start or post-end events from being counted as qualification evidence

reviewers.preferred: reject mixed transport/topology/SHA, duplicate run IDs, stale reports, future-dated provenance beyond bounded skew, and malformed campaign boundaries
reviewers.reason: prevents valid-looking aggregates from being assembled from unrelated, simulated, stale, clock-manipulated, or out-of-frame evidence

reviewers.preferred: offline deterministic aggregation and validation instead of extra qrexec probes or a telemetry daemon
reviewers.reason: adds no worker round trips, negligible CPU/memory overhead, and no production coordinator or mission-queue semantics

alternatives.name: single long campaign
alternatives.correctness: acceptable but couples all fault scenarios and latency samples into one fragile execution
alternatives.robustness: lower because one environment interruption invalidates the entire qualification
alternatives.regressionRisk: medium due to more complex campaign state

alternatives.name: blindly concatenate raw event streams
alternatives.correctness: poor because campaign_start/end and provenance boundaries conflict

alternatives.name: central telemetry/database qualification service
alternatives.regressionRisk: higher operational surface before real Qubes evidence exists

alternatives.name: deterministic multi-run offline aggregator with strict framing and clock-skew checks
alternatives.robustness: fail-closed on incomplete provenance, duplicate run IDs, mixed topology/SHA, missing scenario coverage, insufficient samples, stale/future runs, or evidence outside campaign boundaries
alternatives.latency: linear offline pass only; no qrexec calls added
alternatives.regressionRisk: low because production worker/coordinator semantics are untouched

tests: three independent runs can jointly satisfy recovery, QA-join, and lease-fencing evidence
mixed commit SHA or Qubes topology is rejected
too few runs or latency samples fail closed
a stale member run fails qualification even if the aggregate endpoint looks recent
future-dated runs beyond bounded clock skew fail closed
events before campaign_start or after campaign_end are rejected
missing aggregate scenario coverage fails closed
JSON input accepts event arrays or JSONL campaign strings
GitHub Node QA explicitly runs QA-join evidence, real-worker evidence, and multi-run qualification suites
qa.ciRequirement: Node QA and Swift QA must both be green on the exact new head before Qubes qualification evidence is accepted.

failuresAndLessons: Zero correctness counters are not enough; the qualification must prove that required scenarios were actually exercised across the run set.
Sample aggregation must preserve per-run provenance rather than synthesize one unverifiable campaign.
Freshness must be evaluated for every member run, not only the newest aggregate timestamp.
Freshness checks must reject future-dated provenance beyond a bounded clock-skew allowance; clamping negative age to zero can otherwise accept clock-manipulated evidence.
Qualification evidence must be strictly framed: campaign_start first, campaign_end last, exactly once each.
A green sharded CI result is only meaningful if every readiness test suite is explicitly included in the shard; package-level npm test coverage alone does not guarantee the workflow ran those files.
Real Qubes execution evidence remains mandatory; this aggregator cannot turn simulation into REAL-WORKER READY evidence.
